decisions.check_result: Re-read ws_live (backend/app.py:538-573): user_from_websocket (546) and resolve_camera (554) run once before the while True loop (566-571), which receives frames and calls _process_frame (527-535) with the captured user and camera; _process_frame inserts events (533) and calls dispatch_live_alert (534), which triggers the actuator (375) behind only a global per-level cooldown (370). user_from_token (backend/auth.py:155-160) enforces revoked_at, expires_at and status, but only at connect. manage.py set-password (178) and set-status (184-189) and logout (backend/app.py:463) only update session rows; there is no socket registry or close path besides the pre-loop checks. engine.py:146 emits events for MEDIO/ALTO frames. No source control refutes the claim, and the boundary (a suspended or revoked principal continuing to write community events and drive the shared siren/Telegram) is concrete. Persistence of the open socket after revocation is runtime behaviour that cannot be confirmed without execution, and deployment socket lifetime (uvicorn keepalive, Caddy stream handling) is unconfigured in source, so needs_validation is kept. Trace lines verified; evidence on Dockerfile:25 and Caddyfile:2 added for the lifetime blocker, and the local plan was tightened (stub new_session, wait past the cooldown).

Re-read authenticate (backend/auth.py:85-123): unknown/inactive accounts run verify_password against _DUMMY_HASH (104), the wrong-password path runs verify_password against the user hash (108), but the locked branch returns at 107 with no bcrypt work. _DUMMY_HASH (66) and every user hash (hash_password at 53, the only hash writer per git grep; manage.py 88/176 use it) use bcrypt.gensalt() default cost, so only the locked path lacks the roughly bcrypt-length delay. login_submit (backend/app.py:438-453) returns the identical 401 for all failures, and the code comments (auth.py:64, app.py:450) state that existence must not be inferable, so this defeats a stated control rather than being design-intended. The per-IP throttle (app.py:440, auth.py:34-35) limits but does not remove the oracle. The impact is limited to account-existence disclosure, with a lockout side effect. The timing gap is a runtime measurement not performed here, so the verdict stays needs_validation with a bounded local plan. The trace was reordered so the lock-setting update (auth.py:112) precedes the lookup and the sink, and the unknown-path bcrypt line moved to evidence.

Re-read client_ip (backend/auth.py:253-268): if the TCP peer is in any range of _REDES_DE_CONFIANZA (239-240: 127/8, ::1, 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, fc00::/7), the last X-Forwarded-For element is returned. It keys throttled/register_failure (app.py:440/449, auth.py:283), sessions.ip (app.py:454) and the view_camera audit IP (app.py:731). Through Caddy (Caddyfile:2) the last element is Caddy-set, so that path is safe. docker-compose.yml:10 publishes 8000 on all interfaces and backend/Dockerfile:25 runs plain uvicorn, so whether a direct client is seen as a private peer (userland-proxy/IPv6, rootless Docker, a shared VPC) and whether port 8000 is reachable are deployment facts outside source that decide the claim. The verdict stays needs_validation. The deployment plan was rewritten to be observation-only (firewall/security group, docker info and daemon.json, and existing sessions.ip values and log lines) instead of sending a login request to production.
